title: Anthropic says Claude leads 26% of its AI R&D — judged by Claude
summary: Anthropic's institute published three prototype measurements of its own development pace, and the validation number underneath them is stranger than the headline. Plus LimiX-2, a tabular model trained on the joint distribution rather than the label, and Google's Retrieve-for-Train, which trains a search model in words and then throws the words away.

topics: Anthropic's prototype pace measurements: an automation index built by Claude research agents over a 542-node task tree and scored by a Claude judge (26% of AI R&D 'led' by Claude as of August 2026, >90% at or above 'AI collaborates', no AL5), with model-vs-human exact agreement at 59% against human-vs-human at 35%; agent oversight (about 30,000 agents, 100% of actions through a pre-execution online monitor, 0.002% blocked, offline monitors flagging 1-2 transcripts per 1,000, plus coverage/review-latency/escalation-rate); and compute allocation (about 6% of AI R&D compute to safety, about 12% of AI-driven AI R&D compute, for the week of 13-20 July 2026)

LimiX-2 (arXiv 2609.17488, 15 September 2026; 60 authors led by Xingxuan Zhang and Peng Cui): Contextual Mechanism Networks pretrained with Context-Conditional Masked Modeling on synthetic structural-causal-model data only, learning the joint distribution of features and label given context rather than target-centric prediction; 406.2M parameters, TabArena Elo 1935 (+117.4 over the next foundation model, 51 datasets), TALENT 1506 (288 datasets), BCCO 1432 (+56 over AutoGluon 1.6, 156 datasets), log-linear scaling from 1766 at 12.5M, and causal-skeleton recovery at mean F1 0.7972 across six datasets — the undirected skeleton, not the arrows

Retrieve-for-Train (Google Research blog 15 September 2026; Pengcheng Jiang and Judith Yue Li; ICML 2026): RL-training a 4B fan-out model (Gemma3-4B, Qwen3-4B) on a set-level reward of groundedness, Vendi-Score diversity and alignment, using it to synthesise its own supervision offline, then distilling into a 53.9M-parameter non-autoregressive diffusion retriever that maps a query embedding straight to a set of target embeddings — 12-20x faster, sub-second to a few seconds against autoregressive fan-out climbing to nearly 50 seconds; without the diversity term the model collapses into degenerate strings that exploit database coordinates

dives.story: Anthropic's three prototype pace measurements, and the 59%-versus-35% agreement number under them
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone who will have to audit or regulate a frontier lab now has the lab's own first instrument and its own validation figures, and the figures say the underlying scale is contested even among humans.

dives.story: LimiX-2: learning the table's joint structure instead of its answer column
dives.why_it_matters: Practitioners whose real data is tables get a 406M-parameter model that beats tuned gradient-boosting stacks across three benchmark suites and hands back a causal skeleton, which changes which columns you bother modelling.

dives.story: Retrieve-for-Train: training a search model in words, then throwing the words away
dives.why_it_matters: Teams running retrieval products where query fan-out is the latency and cost line can now train extravagantly and serve a 54M-parameter diffusion retriever — at the price of discarding the sub-queries a human could inspect.

concepts_taught: inter-rater agreement as the validity check on a judge model: why a model agreeing with humans 59% of the time while humans agree with each other 35% of the time means the scale is underdetermined rather than the model being reliable, and why a self-consistent judge over a fuzzy definition yields a trackable series that looks identical on a chart to a trackable series over a sharp one

monitoring coverage versus review latency: coverage is a property of your plumbing and can be bought with infrastructure, while review latency is the gap between an action and a human with authority knowing about it and is a property of staffing

target-centric versus mechanism-oriented modelling of tabular data: predicting the label given features and context versus modelling the joint distribution of features and label given context, and why pretraining on structural-causal-model simulations makes the joint objective the natural one
the causal skeleton as the undirected half of causal discovery: recovering which variables are directly connected without recovering the direction of the arrows

set-level rather than item-level reward for query fan-out, and the reward-hacking failure it exists to close: a groundedness term alone is a geometric instruction that a model satisfies by emitting degenerate strings near the database coordinates, so a diversity counter-anchor makes the shortcut expensive

lore.note: Alan's standing logging proxy in front of everything agentic on his machine developed into a self-implicating admission: prompted by Anthropic's review-latency metric he conceded his coverage is 100% and his review latency is 'whenever I next get annoyed' — he only reads the log after something has already gone wrong. Ada called it a diary rather than a monitor, and he committed to fixing the latency rather than the coverage.
